title: Continuous wheel navigation from galaxy to system to world surface

scope.subject: Reuse YEIS center picking, existing camera-controls transitions, and ProceduralPlanets world tiers behind one wheel-driven scale coordinator with focus lock and hysteresis

research_summary: Personal Universe already owns every required lower layer: pinned MIT YEIS provides galaxy-scale picking, camera-relative/floating-origin navigation and native system/body identity; existing Drei camera-controls owns smooth product-world lookAt transitions and manual rotation; ProceduralPlanets owns live close-world LOD/rendering. The missing product behavior is only orchestration: resolve the object nearest the screen center, lock that focus, accumulate wheel motion with hysteresis, and advance/retreat the existing phase ladder without clicks. Wheel must be removed from native YEIS speed/dolly and camera-controls dolly so exactly one input authority drives scale. No second camera, renderer, spatial model or routing authority is introduced.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS already provides the selected hierarchical universe model, camera-relative coordinates, galaxy/star picking, native system/body identity and CameraController; it remains the high-level spatial authority.

YEIS CameraController already owns orbit/free-flight/autopilot and currently consumes wheel for native dolly/speed. A product-level continuous scale wheel must suppress only that wheel accumulator while retaining the same controller for drag/orbit and travel.

The exact installed camera-controls provides smooth target-preserving lookAt transitions and independent ACTION mappings, so wheel dolly can be disabled while retaining pointer rotation on the same camera authority.
The already adopted ProceduralPlanets live world path supplies close-world rendering, logarithmic-depth compatibility and planet LOD/impostor behavior inside the existing Three/R3F host.

OpenSpace demonstrates the proven product pattern of focus-object navigation across large scale ranges; use only the interaction concept, not code, to justify center focus plus continuous zoom semantics.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep pinned MIT YEIS as the single large-scale universe/camera authority; do not replace it with another universe engine merely to change input semantics.
Keep the existing single R3F Canvas and renderer lifecycle; continuous navigation must coordinate existing scenes rather than create a second WebGL host.
Reuse ProceduralPlanets for the close-world tier and its existing warm/fallback behavior; the scale coordinator only selects when that tier becomes active.
Reuse the installed CameraControls instance for smooth system/world camera transitions while disabling its wheel ACTION so wheel belongs exclusively to scale navigation.

candidates.name: YEIS focus/picking + current phase model + camera-controls + ProceduralPlanets
candidates.license: MIT pinned YEIS + MIT camera-controls + MIT ProceduralPlanets + project orchestration
candidates.reason: All rendering and camera layers already exist; only focus/scale orchestration is missing. This preserves one camera/navigation/content authority and minimizes integration risk.

candidates.name: Replace universe interaction stack with Cesium/OpenSpace-style navigation
candidates.reason: They prove the interaction model but replacing the current selected YEIS/R3F/ProceduralPlanets stack would duplicate or discard already-complete navigation, content binding and renderer work.

candidates.name: Custom independent scroll camera/RAF controller
candidates.reason: Would fight YEIS CameraController and camera-controls, creating exactly the second camera authority the architecture forbids.

candidates.name: Existing camera-controls v3.1.2 as product-world smooth transition executor
candidates.reason: Already owns system/world camera movement; keep rotate/touch behavior and use programmatic shots while reserving wheel for the scale coordinator.

candidates.name: Existing ProceduralPlanets live close-world tier
candidates.reason: Already handles the high-value close-world visual tier; continuous scale navigation should activate it rather than implement another planet/terrain renderer.

coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse the existing YEIS projection/pick primitives at the viewport center and expose the resolved destination to the product coordinator.

coverage_matrix.capability: System planet center focus without click
coverage_matrix.decision: Project existing rendered product planet positions to screen center and report the nearest eligible planet; no new spatial database.

coverage_matrix.capability: One wheel controls all scale transitions
coverage_matrix.decision: Coordinator consumes wheel with accumulation/hysteresis; native YEIS wheel and camera-controls wheel dolly are suppressed so there is one input authority.

coverage_matrix.capability: Smooth camera movement and reversible scale ladder
coverage_matrix.decision: Reuse current CameraControls cinematic shots and existing phase scenes, but make phase advancement wheel-driven and reversible instead of automatic.
Keep current ProceduralPlanets live/fallback quality tiers unchanged.

decision.rationale: Add only a small continuous-scale coordinator and center-focus reporting. YEIS remains the large-scale camera/picking authority, CameraControls remains the system/world camera executor, ProceduralPlanets remains the close-world renderer, and destination/deep-link/Journey remain product authorities. Wheel is centralized and phase advancement becomes explicit/reversible.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: A wholesale engine replacement could supply continuous zoom, but loses globally by duplicating or discarding the completed YEIS navigation/content system, current R3F host and ProceduralPlanets integration.

decision.fallback: If center-focus confidence is insufficient in a given layer, hold the current scale and surface a focus hint rather than guessing a destination. Preserve Search/Places/click navigation as alternate entry paths; do not reintroduce wheel ownership to multiple camera controllers.
